evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Another One Rides the Bus': recorded live on Dr. Demento's radio show on 14 September 1980, parodying Queen's 'Another One Bites the Dust', with Jon 'Bermuda' Schwartz beating Yankovic's accordion case for drums because there was no kit. Self-released on an EP in 1981 and then issued as a single by TK Records in February 1981. Brian May later called it an extremely funny record. The edge year is the broadcast; the track year is the release.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Queen's record runs on John Deacon's bass line and a dry, heavy beat. Yankovic's version replaces the whole band with an accordion and a drummer hitting the accordion's case, recorded live on the radio. Listen for the bass line turned into accordion, and for how much of a crowded bus the lyrics fit in.

explanation.age13: Weird Al made 'Another One Rides the Bus' live on a radio show in 1980, with a friend keeping the beat by hitting his accordion case. It makes fun of Queen's 'Another One Bites the Dust'. Brian May, Queen's guitarist, later said he found it hilarious.
explanation.adult: Made with almost nothing, live on air, and released twice in 1981. The man hitting the case, Jon Schwartz, became Yankovic's long-time drummer.
